Specification: A collection of formal definitions and theorems regarding well-founded induction in TLA+. It formalises concepts like well-founded relations, transitive closures, and inductive definitions, providing theorems for well-founded induction and the unique existence of inductively defined functions.
TheoremNames: LEMMA EmptyIsWellFounded == \A S : IsWellFoundedOn({}, S)
LEMMA IsWellFoundedOnSubset == ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW T \in SUBSET S, IsWellFoundedOn(R,S) PROVE  IsWellFoundedOn(R,T)
LEMMA IsWellFoundedOnSubrelation == ASSUME NEW S, NEW R, NEW RR, RR \cap (S \X S) \subseteq R, IsWellFoundedOn(R,S) PROVE  IsWellFoundedOn(RR,S)
THEOREM WFMin == ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, IsWellFoundedOn(R, S), NEW T, T \subseteq S, T # {} PROVE  \E x \in T : \A y \in T : ~ (<<y, x>> \in R)
THEOREM MinWF == ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, \A T \in SUBSET S : T # {} => \E x \in T : \A y \in T : ~ (<<y, x>> \in R) PROVE  IsWellFoundedOn(R,S)
LEMMA WellFoundedIsIrreflexive == ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW x \in S, IsWellFoundedOn(R, S) PROVE  <<x, x>> \notin R
LEMMA WellFoundedIsAsymmetric == ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW x \in S, NEW y \in S, IsWellFoundedOn(R,S), <<x,y>> \in R, <<y,x>> \in R PROVE  FALSE
LEMMA WFSetLessThanIrreflexive == ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW x \in S, IsWellFoundedOn(R,S) PROVE  x \notin SetLessThan(x,R,S)
LEMMA SetLessTransitive == ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW x \in S, NEW y \in SetLessThan(x,R,S), IsTransitivelyClosedOn(R, S) PROVE  SetLessThan(y, R, S) \subseteq SetLessThan(x, R, S)
THEOREM WFInduction == ASSUME NEW P(_), NEW R, NEW S, IsWellFoundedOn(R, S), \A x \in S : (\A y \in SetLessThan(x, R, S) : P(y)) => P(x) PROVE  \A x \in S : P(x)
THEOREM WFDefOnUnique == ASSUME NEW Def( *,* ), NEW R, NEW S, IsWellFoundedOn(R, S), WFDefOn(R, S, Def) PROVE  WFInductiveUnique(S, Def)

LEMMA WFInductiveDefLemma == ASSUME NEW Def( *,* ), NEW R, NEW S, NEW f, IsWellFoundedOn(R, S), IsTransitivelyClosedOn(R, S), WFDefOn(R, S, Def), OpDefinesFcn(f, S, Def) PROVE  WFInductiveDefines(f, S, Def)
LEMMA TransitiveClosureThm == \A R, S : /\ R \cap S \X S \subseteq TransitiveClosureOn(R, S) /\ IsTransitivelyClosedOn(TransitiveClosureOn(R, S), S)
LEMMA TransitiveClosureMinimal == ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW U \in SUBSET (S \X S), R \cap S \X S \subseteq U, IsTransitivelyClosedOn(U,S) PROVE  TransitiveClosureOn(R,S) \subseteq U
LEMMA TCTCTC == ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW i \in S, NEW j \in S, NEW k \in S, <<i,j>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S), <<j,k>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S) PROVE  <<i,k>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S)
LEMMA TCRTC == ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW i \in S, NEW j \in S, NEW k \in S, <<i,j>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S), <<j,k>> \in R PROVE  <<i,k>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S)
LEMMA RTCTC == ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW i \in S, NEW j \in S, NEW k \in S, <<i,j>> \in R, <<j,k>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S) PROVE  <<i,k>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S)

LEMMA TransitiveClosureChopLast == ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW i \in S, NEW k \in S, <<i,k>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S) PROVE  \E j \in S : /\ <<j,k>> \in R /\ i = j / <<i,j>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S)
THEOREM TransitiveClosureWF == ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, IsWellFoundedOn(R,S) PROVE  IsWellFoundedOn(TransitiveClosureOn(R, S), S)
THEOREM WFInductiveDef == ASSUME NEW Def( *,* ), NEW R, NEW S, NEW f, IsWellFoundedOn(R, S), WFDefOn(R, S, Def), OpDefinesFcn(f, S, Def) PROVE  WFInductiveDefines(f, S, Def)

THEOREM WFInductiveDefType == ASSUME NEW Def( *,* ), NEW f, NEW R, NEW S, NEW T, T # {}, IsWellFoundedOn(R, S), WFDefOn(R, S, Def), WFInductiveDefines(f, S, Def), \A g \in [S -> T], s \in S : Def(g, s) \in T PROVE  f \in [S -> T]
THEOREM NatLessThanWellFounded == IsWellFoundedOn(OpToRel(<,Nat), Nat)
THEOREM PreImageWellFounded == ASSUME NEW S, NEW T, NEW R, NEW f(_), \A s \in S : f(s) \in T, IsWellFoundedOn(R, T) PROVE  IsWellFoundedOn(PreImage(f, S, R), S)
THEOREM WFLexPairOrdering == ASSUME NEW R1, NEW R2, NEW S1, NEW S2, IsWellFoundedOn(R1, S1), IsWellFoundedOn(R2, S2) PROVE  IsWellFoundedOn(LexPairOrdering(R1, R2, S1, S2), S1 \X S2)
THEOREM WFLexProductOrdering == ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW n \in Nat, IsWellFoundedOn(R, S) PROVE  IsWellFoundedOn(LexProductOrdering(R, S, n), [1..n -> S])
SetEnumeration: { ss \in S \X S : \A U \in SUBSET (S \X S) : /\ R \cap S \X S \subseteq U /\ IsTransitivelyClosedOn(U, S) => ss \in U }
{ss \in (S1 \X S2) \X (S1 \X S2) : / <<ss, ss>> \in R1 / /\ ss = ss /\ <<ss, ss>> \in R2}
ChoiceExpr: CHOOSE g : g = [x \in S |-> Def(g, x)]
AssumeProveBlocks: ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW T \in SUBSET S, IsWellFoundedOn(R,S) PROVE  IsWellFoundedOn(R,T)
ASSUME NEW S, NEW R, NEW RR, RR \cap (S \X S) \subseteq R, IsWellFoundedOn(R,S) PROVE  IsWellFoundedOn(RR,S)
ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, IsWellFoundedOn(R, S), NEW T, T \subseteq S, T # {} PROVE  \E x \in T : \A y \in T : ~ (<<y, x>> \in R)
ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, \A T \in SUBSET S : T # {} => \E x \in T : \A y \in T : ~ (<<y, x>> \in R) PROVE  IsWellFoundedOn(R,S)
ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW x \in S, IsWellFoundedOn(R, S) PROVE  <<x, x>> \notin R
ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW x \in S, NEW y \in S, IsWellFoundedOn(R,S), <<x,y>> \in R, <<y,x>> \in R PROVE  FALSE
ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW x \in S, IsWellFoundedOn(R,S) PROVE  x \notin SetLessThan(x,R,S)
ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW x \in S, NEW y \in SetLessThan(x,R,S), IsTransitivelyClosedOn(R, S) PROVE  SetLessThan(y, R, S) \subseteq SetLessThan(x, R, S)
ASSUME NEW P(_), NEW R, NEW S, IsWellFoundedOn(R, S), \A x \in S : (\A y \in SetLessThan(x, R, S) : P(y)) => P(x) PROVE  \A x \in S : P(x)
ASSUME NEW Def( *,* ), NEW R, NEW S, IsWellFoundedOn(R, S), WFDefOn(R, S, Def) PROVE  WFInductiveUnique(S, Def)
ASSUME NEW Def( *,* ), NEW R, NEW S, NEW f, IsWellFoundedOn(R, S), IsTransitivelyClosedOn(R, S), WFDefOn(R, S, Def), OpDefinesFcn(f, S, Def) PROVE  WFInductiveDefines(f, S, Def)
ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW U \in SUBSET (S \X S), R \cap S \X S \subseteq U, IsTransitivelyClosedOn(U,S) PROVE  TransitiveClosureOn(R,S) \subseteq U
ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW i \in S, NEW j \in S, NEW k \in S, <<i,j>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S), <<j,k>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S) PROVE  <<i,k>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S)
ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW i \in S, NEW j \in S, NEW k \in S, <<i,j>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S), <<j,k>> \in R PROVE  <<i,k>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S)
ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW i \in S, NEW j \in S, NEW k \in S, <<i,j>> \in R, <<j,k>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S) PROVE  <<i,k>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S)
ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW i \in S, NEW k \in S, <<i,k>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S) PROVE  \E j \in S : /\ <<j,k>> \in R /\ i = j / <<i,j>> \in TransitiveClosureOn(R,S)
ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, IsWellFoundedOn(R,S) PROVE  IsWellFoundedOn(TransitiveClosureOn(R, S), S)
ASSUME NEW Def( *,* ), NEW R, NEW S, NEW f, IsWellFoundedOn(R, S), WFDefOn(R, S, Def), OpDefinesFcn(f, S, Def) PROVE  WFInductiveDefines(f, S, Def)
ASSUME NEW Def( *,* ), NEW f, NEW R, NEW S, NEW T, T # {}, IsWellFoundedOn(R, S), WFDefOn(R, S, Def), WFInductiveDefines(f, S, Def), \A g \in [S -> T], s \in S : Def(g, s) \in T PROVE  f \in [S -> T]
ASSUME NEW S, NEW T, NEW R, NEW f(_), \A s \in S : f(s) \in T, IsWellFoundedOn(R, T) PROVE  IsWellFoundedOn(PreImage(f, S, R), S)
ASSUME NEW R1, NEW R2, NEW S1, NEW S2, IsWellFoundedOn(R1, S1), IsWellFoundedOn(R2, S2) PROVE  IsWellFoundedOn(LexPairOrdering(R1, R2, S1, S2), S1 \X S2)
ASSUME NEW R, NEW S, NEW n \in Nat, IsWellFoundedOn(R, S) PROVE  IsWellFoundedOn(LexProductOrdering(R, S, n), [1..n -> S])
